name: navigation-menu

frames.best_why: Products panel is open with all three two-line links visible and no cursor blocking the text.

tagline: Header links whose chevrons drop a panel of sub-pages.
summary: A short horizontal menu of top-level links where Products and Docs carry chevrons and open a bordered panel of two-line destinations. Hovering a trigger highlights it and flips its chevron while the panel slides in.
appearance: Three light grey links in a row on black, with small chevrons after Products and Docs. An open trigger gets a soft grey rounded background, and a dark bordered panel drops below holding bold titles stacked over muted description lines.
behaviour: Hovering or clicking a trigger opens its panel with a short slide and fade while the chevron turns upward; moving to another trigger swaps the panel in place. Clicking outside closes it.
demo_content: Products lists Overview, Analytics and Integrations; Docs lists Getting Started and API Reference; Pricing is plain.
search_phrases: menu bar for a website header
hover to reveal a list of pages
products and docs tabs with chevrons
use_when: A header needs a few top-level destinations whose contents are worth previewing in a panel.
avoid_when: Panels open on hover, so touch users must tap and the panel then covers page content.
customise: You build the row from items, triggers, panels and links, each taking classes; turning viewport off anchors each panel to its own trigger instead of a shared box.
weight_why: A few links and one floating panel; nothing runs while the menu is closed.

a11y.note: Triggers open by hover, click or keyboard and roles come from the primitive, but the slide and zoom ignore reduced-motion settings.

issues: The demo omits the small indicator arrow that the source exports
The menu floats alone on a black page, so it is not shown in a real header
polish_why: Clean, legible menu with a smooth panel swap; plain styling and no header context around it.
